text:
samir: Heads-up — finance noticed several small negative invoice adjustments in the dashboard for yesterday's midnight batch. Looks like some usage got applied after invoice generation. Anyone seen late 'usage_reconcile' events land?

maria: saw one alert from the metering job about a Kafka partition lag spike around 00:05 UTC. could be related.

kevin: I think this is the watermarking behavior — compaction + out-of-order writes meant some per-session token totals arrived after the invoice cutoff. we currently backfill by emitting "usage_reconcile" events that subtract/adjust.

lisa: dashboard shows 43 negative-line items across 28 customers, all very small (<$2). not catastrophic but annoying and confusing for customers.

praveen: question: are those adjustments coming from router-level retries or from intermediate enrichment? router emits first, enrichment does model-name attachment later which triggers a second event in the pipeline.

samir: good call — initial trace for acct 0x3c shows two usage events: one minimal token count at 23:59:58 and then an enriched record at 00:06:12. invoice cutoff was 00:00. invoice service picked the early event but reconcile subtract came later.

kevin: that's the core problem: we use event timestamps for invoice window but rely on commit order for dedupe in the downstream aggregator. compaction + reorder on topic 'metering.enriched' means reconciles can show up later.

maria: ingest-bot: can you show partition lag / offsets for that day?

ingest-bot: partition lag spike for topic metering.raw at 2026-03-12T00:04: failed broker restart -> consumer group 'enrich-workers' lagged ~120k msgs for ~3m.

lisa: finance wants either (A) move invoice cutoff back by 5m to include late enrich events, (B) change reconcile semantics so adjustments are batched into next invoice cycle without negative lines, or (C) fix upstream so enrich never creates duplicate post-cutoff events.

praveen: (A) is simpler operationally but shifts SLA and delays invoices. (B) is product UX change — we'd convert negative adjustments into 'credit' line on next invoice; need legal sign-off. (C) is best long-term but could be hairy (make enrich idempotent + preserve original order).

kevin: technical note: we can emit reconciles with an 'effective_time' that is the original usage ts and let billing apply a 'late flag' and choose to either retroactively patch invoice or roll into next period. billing API currently only supports point-in-time apply.

samir: I propose short-term: add a 10-minute sliding window during invoice generation to query "enrich" topic for any late events with same session_id and apply them before finalizing invoice (opt-in flag per-account).

maria: agree for canary: we can opt-in for small subset of high-touch customers to avoid surprise. I'll add a console toggle under Billing -> Invoice behavior for 'Include late enrich events (10m window)'.

lisa: coord with finance to enable for 5 customers and monitor. create dashboard: negative line count, backfill count, average reconcile amount.

praveen: long-term, we should change enrich to attach model metadata at ingest time (router) to avoid the two-step emit. that's a bigger change for eng-runtime and routers.

kevin: I'll open an RFC for that model-attachment-at-ingest plan and include metrics for complexity/cost.

samir: action items: kevin -> RFC + short-term ad-hoc 10m window PR; maria -> console toggle and canary config; lisa -> finance sign-off + dashboard queries; praveen -> assess router changes. I can help wire the canary rollout policy.

maria: I'll start the console PR and wire the flag to billing job. will tag you all. :thumbsup:

lisa: thanks everyone. ping if you see any new negative adjustments while we test.

kevin: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/412 "billing: query enrich window before invoice finalize (10m canary)"

samir: nice. let's keep the canary to low-risk customers and monitor.

ingest-bot: deploy to canary cluster started for pr 412 at 2026-03-13T02:10 UTC.

maria: canary shows reduction in negative-lines on first run. posting follow-up numbers in #eng-platform after next midnight run.

lisa: closing loop: finance ok with canary approach. will schedule legal review for credit-line UX change.

samir: closing thread for now, escalating router-model-attach to RFC board. thanks all.
